Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure.
  - New wheeze with shortness of breath beginning after house cleaning with dust exposure from carpet; patient suspects dust may be a trigger.
- Symptom timeline and progression.
  - Onset ~1 hour after dust exposure; duration 2 days; worse at night; reports worsening over the two days.
- ENT symptoms (as applicable): throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face), ear/neck symptoms.
  - Throat swelling/closure: not reported.
  - Voice change: not reported.
  - Dysphagia/odynophagia: not reported.
  - Drooling: not reported.
  - Nasal/ocular symptoms: history of seasonal hay fever; no current nasal/ocular symptoms documented.
  - Stridor/noisy breathing: wheeze reported.
  - Dyspnea: yes; sometimes unable to complete sentences when talking.
  - Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: not reported.
  - Ear/neck symptoms: not reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments (including any prior hospital care or injection therapy).
  - Childhood asthma; occasional exercise-related wheeze as an adult.
  - Has taken oral steroids previously for asthma (details not provided).
  - No prior emergency department visits or injection therapies mentioned.
- Allergies and current medications (mark missing dose/route/frequency as not documented).
  - Allergies: none known reported.
  - Medications: “asthma inhaler” at home from a couple of months ago; dose/route/frequency not documented. Patient has not used it for the current episode.
  - No antihistamines at home; does not usually take medication for hay fever.
- Any relevant social context (e.g., accompaniment/supervision).
  - Consult conducted while patient was in a private space at home.
  - Reports GP/doctor’s surgery is a short drive away (exact time not clearly stated).

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution (e.g., lips, tongue, uvula, face) if stated.
  - None reported.
- Airway/breathing descriptors if stated (e.g., stridor, work of breathing).
  - Patient-reported wheeze and shortness of breath; sometimes cannot complete sentences during conversation. No chest pain with deep breath.
- Mental status and associated features (e.g., dizziness, syncope) if stated.
  - Alert; no dizziness reported.
- Vitals and examination findings only if mentioned; otherwise note “Not recorded.”
  - Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient (if stated).
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Suspected asthma exacerbation likely triggered by dust exposure; allergic component possible.
- Justification: onset ~1 hour post dust exposure; progressive wheeze and dyspnea over 2 days, worse at night; history of childhood asthma and seasonal hay fever; intermittent difficulty completing sentences; no throat swelling, voice change, or facial/oral swelling reported.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Advised in-person evaluation at GP/clinic for assessment including pulse oximetry.
  - Clinician to send a letter to GP via the app summarizing this consultation.
  - May require a course of steroids pending in-person assessment.
- Medications/instructions:
  - If available, take an over-the-counter antihistamine prior to/while going to the clinic; if not available, GP can prescribe.
- Specific instructions provided to patient/caregiver:
  - Attend GP/clinic in person for prompt assessment.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Not explicitly discussed in transcript.
- Follow-up:
  - In-person GP review planned; further management (e.g., steroids) to be determined after assessment.
  - No allergy/ENT referral discussed.
- COVID-19 vaccine suitability:
  - Not discussed.

Quality checks:
- Missing clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs, oxygen saturation, or peak flow/spirometry recorded.
  - Type and dosing of “asthma inhaler” not documented; no use during this episode.
  - No detailed allergy list beyond “none known”; no anaphylaxis screening plan or auto-injector discussion.
  - No clear safety-netting/red-flag instructions (e.g., worsening breathlessness, inability to speak full sentences, cyanosis, chest pain, throat swelling).
  - No smoking history or environmental exposures beyond dust documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - None noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Occasional audio/video disruption; some responses truncated (e.g., distance to surgery). Clinical detail limited by teleconsult and lack of examination.
